source.title: Decided Upstream, Written Late: Locating and Pricing the Cross-Lingual Refusal Circuit of a Multilingual MoE

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It measures harmful-versus-benign difference-in-means directions and intervenes on them to test refusal, but uses repeated decode-step activation addition rather than the original all-layer ablation and addition procedure. It also reports evidence refining the single-direction account.
record.gate_note: The paper reports activation steering, direction geometry, behavioral recovery, and intervention results on the attributed refusal circuit. Values used in choosing axes or layers are included only when they also report a result relevant to a tested version. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study builds an Arditi-style harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means axis in Sarvam-30B, a reasoning MoE, and steers with it. That addition bears on V1 and V8. It also measures the axis's cross-language alignment (V6) and its orthogonality to a refused-minus-complied refusal axis (V5). It does not ablate the direction, and it does not use the original all-layer addition, so it is T2 rather than T1. The writer/opposer circuit results concern components, not directions, and do not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add that the authors state the upstream harm direction causally controls refusal when re-applied over generation, and that the cross-lingual gap is not a detection failure. Also add their findings that damping the opposer is cheap and effective, amplifying the writer is a cost wall, and surgical head edits are inert.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means axes, but tests repeated decode-step activation addition rather than the original all-layer projection ablation and refusal-direction addition. It also constructs and analyzes an independent output-position refused-minus-complied direction.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering depends on decode-step repetition and hook layer: single-pass injection does not move the L15–18 output band; repeated steering has strong leverage at L5–10 and drops sharply past L11–12. The measured circuit-edit effects also vary by component, dose, and model architecture.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-lingual overlap of harm-correlated experts peaks at L11 (0.43) and collapses to null at L18 (0.027), while a category signal stays at 0.117. The same shape is reported in Qwen3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multilingual MoEs share upstream harm routing but use language-specific expert sets near the output.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal logit is written by a late MoE writer opposed by late attention, in Sarvam-30B and Qwen3-30B-A3B. Damping the opposer recovers refusal cheaply; amplifying the writer is costly; surgical head edits are inert.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal output is set by a writer/opposer component circuit whose intervention cost is asymmetric and architecture-dependent.

fits_no_version.finding: An output-position refused-minus-complied direction does not reliably steer refusal (0–1/5). Qwen3 shows a 0.28 vs 0.07 Indic/English compliance gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The causal lever for refusal is the upstream harm direction, not the correlational refusal-outcome direction.

record.peer_reviewed: Workshop on Actionable Interpretability at COLM 2026
record.problems: The paper studies one model in depth and has one cross-model check. Writer-amplification recovery uses a small dose set (n=6) and is described as noisy. Recovery and harm labels rely on an LLM judge; regex agreement is reported, but there is no human adjudication at scale. Surgical-head outputs often did not commit within the generation budget. Upstream steering perplexity was not measured, and the cost map combines heterogeneous evaluation sets.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant behavioral rows omitted. The paper also reports language-probe accuracy and ASCII/script diagnostics, which do not measure the claim versions. The full layer-by-layer single-pass injection sweep is summarized by the explicit L10 and L18 text results in R15–R16; the remaining table entries were not separately extracted because the flattened table header and values do not unambiguously assign every displayed number to a layer.

untested.parts: Ablation of the direction, all-layer addition on harmless prompts, and capability retention under steering (perplexity not measured for upstream steering).
No test of affine, cone or multi-direction structure of refusal itself. The circuit results are component-level.
No base-to-instruct or model-variant transfer of the direction. The Qwen3 check does not reuse or compare the direction.
Ablation in the reasoning model. There is no non-reasoning comparison of the generation-time effect (Qwen3 is non-reasoning but its steering was not run).

missing.what: Single-pass injection lift at L12 (+1.62 nats) and L14 (+0.62 nats) is clearly tabulated, contrary to rows_left_out.
Dose-response of malicious recovery and benign knockout vs α. This would show whether adding the direction induces refusal on benign prompts at higher doses.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. V4 is relabelled not tested: the record's V4 evidence is either harm/refusal separation (V5) or component circuits (fits_no_version). Within-paper inconsistency: L10 α=4 recovery is 0.65 in Section 4 but 80% in the Appendix B sweep. Generation-time findings are Sarvam-only. Labels depend on a Claude Haiku judge (38/39 regex agreement).

versions.untested_parts: Does not ablate the difference-in-means direction. Does not test whether adding it induces refusal to harmless requests as a direct outcome; it reports benign refusal/knockout as collateral. Does not establish that other abilities are largely intact for upstream steering, whose perplexity was unmeasured.
No practical weight edit of the single difference-in-means direction.
Does not test jailbreaks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
Does not directly compare affine, cone, or dominant-direction parameterizations; it reports separate harm-detection and refusal-writing directions and a writer/opposer circuit.
Does not separately evaluate an explicit harmfulness judgment and refusal decision with a dedicated behavioral judgment measure.

Tests cross-language alignment in Sarvam-30B, but does not test transfer from base to instruct models. Qwen3-30B-A3B is checked for circuit organization and intervention effects, not for transfer of the same measured harm direction.
No comparison of refusal training methods, timing, or training stages.
The reasoning-model generation-time findings are for Sarvam-30B only; the non-reasoning Qwen3-30B-A3B check does not test those generation-time claims.
